#### Watching, waiting, drifting 

- The copper price moved sideways in a narrow range in November, lacking any strong signals from the fundamentals.  We expect that this will continue to be the case through to the end of the year, as activity winds down and market participants look ahead to 2013. 

- With negotiations for 2013 annual contracts ongoing between most major producers and consumers of cathode, the spot market is quiet as players are reluctant to “move the market”. In this environment, spot premium levels lack clarity but are believed to be in similar ranges to those quoted a month ago. Meanwhile, Codelco has settled with its Chinese customers for 2013. 

- China’s bonded stocks rose recently, sparking debate on the total levels yet again. We outline our calculations on the total cathode stocks breakdown of the world’s top copper consumer in this issue.

Copper Monitor December 2012 www.crugroup.com #### Copper treading water We forecast in the last monitor that the price would move sideways in November and for the most part this is what we have seen. While there has been more pressure towards the down side, resulting in the LME cash price trading in the range of $7,600-$7,800/t this month compared to an average of $8,070/t in October and $7,864/t in the week of the previous monitor, support has been found at around $7,600/t. An uptrend for the price began mid-month, as the US dollar weakened against the Euro on news of progress on another Greek bailout. Cu price flat in NovemberLME 3M
LME 3M, US$/t, July - November 2012
As noted, however, the price movement has been very Data: LME flat compared to most other months this year. Investors that we have spoken to point out that the red metal’s fundamentals are not providing much in the way of direction, leaving the price to be tossed around on macroeconomic data releases and geopolitical events. Two major political leadership selections this year took place in November, with the result that the incumbent US President Barack Obama was re-elected and the new leaders of China were anointed smoothly. Neither event caused much of a stir for copper, but sentiments on the US market have now turned to the matter of the upcoming “fiscal cliff”, causing some downward pressure on the price during the month. Last week’s data releases revealed more encouraging signals from China and the US, and mixed data from Europe. Investors tended to respond more strongly to the good news and copper rose to start this week above $7,700/t. #### Codelco settles 2013 premiums with Chinese #### customers; other negotiations ongoing News has emerged this week that Codelco has settled its 2013 annual cathode supply contracts with its Chinese customers at a premium level of $98/t. There are also some rumours circulating that contract tonnages have been reduced with certain customers, but not all of our sources are able to confirm the story. In the last month, the Chilean state miner has also agreed 2013 premiums with Japan and Korea at $85/t, which is the same level as its European agreements (as we reported in last month’s monitor). Over in the US, we hear reports that

Codelco has offered 2¢/lb CIF Panama City, Florida, but we are not aware if this has been accepted by customers. This would be a 0.25¢/lb increase on 2012’s premium, so it would be an interesting result given the reductions seen elsewhere, but reports are circulating that other © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 19 Copper Monitor December 2012 www. crugroup.com producers have achieved this number. Some market commentators speculate that the increase could be due to the $1.75¢/lb agreed for this year being seen as too low. Elsewhere, most other major buyers and sellers in the physical market are also conducting their annual contract negotiations for 2013, and so they are avoiding the spot market while this goes on. For this reason, spot premiums are not very visible, with little business being conducted. #### China’s stock levels - how high? Turning to China, much has been made of a report widely circulated last week that stated that Chinese bonded stocks are around 1Mt. We have already outlined our disagreement with this view in last week’s CCF report, but we note that if our estimates of the Shanghai and Guangdong bonded stocks are added to the non-bonded SHFE stocks, then we arrive at a figure of around 961,000t. This is our total estimate of “visible stocks”. On top of this, the invisible stocks, which consist of the State Reserve Bureau’s (SRB’s) reserves and producer/consumer stocks, besides material housed in private warehouses and transit stocks, are believed to add around another 2.3Mt , so CRU estimates that Chinese stocks total somewhere in the region of 3.3Mt. This is clearly a huge volume - given that we estimate consumption in China in 2012 will amount to around 8.1Mt of refined copper, the level equates to around 21 weeks’ worth of consumption. However, of this total we believe that around 1Mt is in the hands of the SRB, who are not believed to be looking to sell any time soon, while the producer/consumer/transit stocks are a Refined copper, Mt, November 2012

necessary part of manufacturing operations and we are informed that consumer stocks have been run down to minimal levels this year. How much of the total is being used as collateral and is intended to remain in the warehouses is therefore the key question in determining how much could potentially come out onto the market. Sources in China believe that around 70% of the stocks in bonded warehouses are used for financing purposes. If we therefore use the assumption that only 30% could come out in the near future, and that the SRB stocks, producer/consumer and transit stocks are also unavailable, then we reduce the volume to around 1.2Mt of ready stocks. This equates to around 8 weeks of consumption, which in our vie

w is highly unlikely to hit the market at once. 

In the market, we understand that Shanghai bonded stocks rose again by around 50,000t to 700,000750,000t, while Guangdong bonded stocks are believed to be unchanged at around 75,000t.  The arbitrage has improved to favour imports but this has clearly not yet driven an increase in stocks moving out of the bonded warehouses.  With the Codelco annual negotiations only just concluded, the market has been quiet and spot premiums are in the range of $30-60/t for imported cathode.

Demand remains somewhat subdued, with surveys by Shanghai Metals Market showing that utilisation rates at the flat-rolled copper and copper tube plants that they monitor declined in October m-o-m. Wirerod utilisation rates, however, were reported to have increased.  We also note that it is the small companies that are most affected, while larger semis producers are maintaining stable activity rates. 

#### Eurozone lurches on, waiting for better times 

The Eurozone’s ongoing debt crisis continues to inspire downbeat headlines, interspersed with occasional glimpses of the sun as progress seems momentarily to be made during one of its drawn-out sets of talks. November’s principal drama surrounded the terms of yet another bailout for the Greek government, which after three rounds of talks was finalised earlier this week.  Markets responded positively to the news, and copper rose to a three-month high.  However, the OECD announced on the same day that it had lowered its 2013 growth forecast for almost the entire European continent, slashing the outlook for Greece, Italy and Spain, which were already expected to experience growth contractions next year. Northern countries were not exempt from the downgrade but they are still expected to grow next year. The OECD announcement is in line with what we are hearing from market participants who see a twospeed Europe emerging, with copper demand holding up better in the Northern bloc and dropping rapidly in the Southern bloc. 

The question remains; when will recovery really begin to kick in?  While many are now looking to 2013 and are no longer focused on the remains of this year, certain pieces of data and anecdotal evidence were more hopeful in November.  The composite PMI released by HSBC/Markit last week showed a twomonth high of 45.8 for this month, with the manufacturing PMI showing an 8-month high of 46.2.  This matches recent conversations with physical market insiders, who have reported experiencing a stronger November for sales.  Semi-fabricated copper producers have described business in November as “good”, albeit in comparison to weak trading conditions in September and October. 

However, semis consumers are still asking for short delivery times and are said to be adopting a “hand-tomouth policy” of ordering only what is needed and keeping stocks very low.  The

worst performing sector is said to be that of flat-rolled copper products, due to the depressed auto industry in southern Europe, while the wirerod sector seems to be picking up.  The general sentiment seems to be that people are waiting and hoping for a better year next year. 

Despite these tougher circumstances for demand, the physical cathode market remains tight for near term delivery due to the LME warehouse queues, allowing spot premiums to remain above $80/t.  However, as noted above, with so little business going on it is difficult to pin down the premiums at this time. Insiders have confirmed to us that the market remains quiet, with no one willing to “move the market” as the year draws to a close. 

LME warehouse tonnages in Europe were static throughout the month at around 43,000-45,000t, but on 19<sup>th</sup> November there was a warrant cancellation of 6,100t for material in the Antwerp warehouses.  This

material is now queuing, and so there has been no meaningful change in visible stocks in Europe this month. 

#### US: Fiscal cliff looms and ETF plans causing a stir 

Meanwhile in the US, the economy continues to look healthier, with construction data showing spending reaching a three-year high in September, and labour data released a month ago that showed 171,000 jobs added in the same month.  2013 is also expected to be a good year for construction, and while we note that most of the construction growth is set to be residential rather than commercial, meaning that copper consumption will be less directly affected, it remains a positive indicator for the country’s economy as a whole.  Other data released on house prices, consumer confidence and durable goods spending also showed an upward trend, and HSBC/Markit’s manufacturing PMI rose to 52.4 for November, compared with 51.0 in October. The cloud on the horizon remains the unresolved “fiscal cliff” situation, with just over a month now to avoid the abrupt tax increases and spending cuts that will swing into effect on January 1<sup>st</sup> unless a new budget deal for 2013 can be reached.  This week, following the country’s Thanksgiving holiday, the lack of a settlement has begun to weigh on the stock market.  A failure to meet the deadline will severely impact the country’s economy next year, hampering copper demand and therefore prices. 

Turning to the physical market, in the last month the SEC has announced that it finds no connection between metals ETF flows and commodity prices, paving the way for the physically-backed copper ETFs proposed by JP Morgan Chase.  This has been challenged by a group of copper traders and consumers, including Southwire, Luvata and Encore Wire, who claim that these funds would remove a significant volume of copper from circulation in the short term, thus constricting supply and raising prices and volatility.  The SEC will rule

on whether to approve the go-ahead of these types of ETFs in December. As in Europe, the market is quiet, which is typical for this time of year. Our sources indicate that most of the larger consumers of copper in the US have restricted themselves to using the material they booked on long term contracts this year, leaving most of the spot activity to be conducted by smaller players buying or selling hundreds of tonnes at a time. With very little business being done in the spot market, premiums are said to have not moved much from the range of 6-7¢/lb. #### Price to drift into 2013 at similar level The vast majority of the conversations we had for this monitor involved investors who are not feeling any strong signals from the fundamentals and physical market participants who are in negotiations and reluctant to make a move on the spot market. The recurrent themes were that of limited activity and “waiting for next year” and so barring a substantial financial upset in the next month, we can only see the copper price continuing to drift sideways as the year draws to an end, broadly in the range of $7,6007,800/t. Thus we expect the price to finish the year in the fashion it has so far progressed; with a flat aspect which has (so far) resulted in the lowest standard deviation in daily prices since 2004, and with any fluctuations that do occur to be mainly caused by global economic news. © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 5 of 19 Copper Monitor December 2012 www.crugroup.com ### Consumption trends #### Soft patch for tube consumption The outlook for global economic growth, and by dint of its end-uses, the outlook for copper tube, still remains mired by the rumbling troubles of the eurozone, and an absent bounce in Q3 Chinese economic growth. Relative to previous years, the third quarter of 2012 held no major negative events. However, the lack of any strong drivers of global demand, and soft patches in some key consuming regions, has led to a decrease in our estimate of copper tube consumption of 3.9% y- o-y to 577,000t in Q3 2012. China, the world’s largest producer and consumer of copper tube, is estimated to have produced 238,800t and consumed 212,000t of copper tube in Q3 2012, a decrease of 0.5% y-o-y and 0.8% y-o-y respectively. copper tube consumption, declined 23.6% y-o-y in the third quarter compared to Q3 2011. However, the same data for household freezers showed an increase of 23.6% y-o-y, and the production of washing machines and household refrigerators showed little change in Q3 versus the previous year. Other driv

ers of copper tube consumption, such as building completions, picked up in Q3 compared to the same period a year ago, with total constructed floor space of commercial building registering an 8.9% y-o-y increase in Q3 2012 and completed floor space of residential buildings registering an 8.6% y-o-y increase.  On balance, we have estimated a small decline in Chinese production and consumption of copper tube as the weakness in air conditioner production was offset by activity in other sectors. 

Data post-Q3 has started to show some signs of a pickup with the latest HSBC/Markit PMI reading for October rising to a 13-month high of 50.4 in October, while production data for home appliances, particularly air conditioners, also improved in the month. 

Of the other regions we monitor, North East Asia showed particular weakness with Q3 copper tube production in Japan and South Korea registering falls of 16% y-o-y and 12% y-o-y respectively, according to data from the **Japan Copper and Brass Association** and Korea’s statistics office.  Japanese exports of copper tube, which were at levels between 9,700t/q and 11,800t/q five years ago, declined last quarter to just 3,700t.  South Korea, which unlike Japan saw its exports of tube hold up reasonably well, saw its apparent tube consumption fall by 18.5% y-o-y, in Q3, indicating weakening domestic demand for tube.

The US was alone amongst the major developed markets in showing resilient production of copper tube. Despite Q3 output falling 5.9% q-o-q from Q2, largely the result of seasonal effects, according to **WBMS** data Q3 output is estimated to be 1.8% y-o-y higher than the same period last year, taking production to 67,100t.  Improving data in the housing sector helped support US consumption of copper tube which increased to 2.6% y-o-y to 79,000t.  Household completions have been on an upward trend, and seasonally adjusted Q3 housing completions posted the strongest quarter since Q2 2010.  The momentum in the construction industry has carried on after Q3 with October housing starts increasing 3.8% m-o-m and coming in at 894,000, the strongest monthly reading since July 2008.  Production in other North American countries was mixed; Canada is estimated to have produced 4,000t of copper tube in Q3, a slight increase from the first half of the year but a 7.0% y-o-y decline from the Q3 2011, whilst production in Mexico increased 14.2% y-o-y to 8,000t. 

Discussing North America as part of the **Mueller Industries** Q3 outlook, CEO Greg Christopher, said "we agree with the many economists who believe the construction industry is in the process of recovery. Most predict that 2013 will be a much better year for housing and thereafter commercial construction.” Mueller’s CEO also noted in their Q3 results that "absent of disruptions..., we should see improved demand levels for our products, espec

ially as we move into the seasonally stronger spring months." The European copper tube market continued to struggle, and CRU estimates that the production of copper tube in the continent fell 2.1% y-o-y in Q3. The north of the continent fared better than the south; however, production has declined across the board in Q3. German production of copper tube is estimated to have registered a 3.2% y-o-y decline in Q3, with the market participants we spoke to saying that the copper tube market was subdued in September and October but not faring a badly as other semis markets. Production in Italy, measured by the WBMS, registered a 5.6% y-o-y decline in Q3 2012 relative to Q3 2011, 13,500t from 14,300t. Spanish production is also expected to have declined over the period as exports contracted an estimated 40% y-o-y in Q3. Producers of copper tube remain reasonably gloomy about the picture for Europe. **KME Group** , the Italian producer of copper tube, revised down its expectations for sales in its Q3 results, stating that the first half of the year “saw a continuation of the decline in sales that started in the second half of 2011 and a third quarter that further confirmed this trend.” **Kobelco Group** , the large Japanese conglomerate that manufactures copper tube as well as other semis, said in their third quarter results that demand for copper tube in Europe during Q3 was “stagnant.” However, one of our contacts at a large European semis producer told us that they had experienced some pickup in November orders. #### Pressure to consolidate builds in China In CRU’s November publications, we have talked about the need for consolidation amongst Chinese producers of semis. In the 29th October - 9th November edition of China Copper Fortnightly, we wrote a focus piece on the wire and cable industry in Dongguan noting that we expect at least 30% of the producers in that region to shut down or merge to survive. An October survey of 21 copper tube © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 7 of 19 Copper Monitor December 2012 www.crugroup.com producers, conducted by the **Shanghai Metals Market** , indicates to us that the tube market in China is also ripe for consolidation. As part of a prospectus for its IPO on the Shanghai stock exchange, **Henan Golden Dragon** reported that **Data: CRU Analysis** its first half profitability in 2012 had increased to RMB68.58M (US$10.92M) from RMB13.08M (US$2.08M) in H1 2011.Despite falls in the company’s utilisation rate, from 96.24% in 2011 to 87.57% in H1 2012, the company’s utilisation rate remains well above the industry sample average reported by SMM. As shown in the chart above, production of copper tube in China has reached a plateau in the last two years, indicating tougher competition as growth rates slow in the sector. Given that larger copper tube producers like Henan Golden Dragon are better financed, have better utilisation rates and thicker profit margins, tougher competition should be a catalyst driving consolidation of smaller producers in the Chinese tube market. #### Alloy RBS consumption a bit firmer According to CRU estimates, world consumption of alloy RBS increased 3.1% in Q3 from a year earlier, led by firmer demand in China and a slight pickup in consumption in some areas of Europe; particularly in Eastern European countries where imports in the quarter increased compared to Q3 2011. Q3 production of Chinese alloy RBS increased moderately by 2.9% y-o-y compared to Q3 2011. This firmer data was not matched elsewhere in North East Asia with output from North East Asian alloy RBS plants remaining flat after two quarters of growth, according to national and industry association data. The US again proved to be a source of better developed market production. According to WBMS data, alloy RBS production at US factories increased by 4.8% in Q3 compared to a year earlier to reach 56,000t. WBMS data for Italian alloy RBS production, which showed an increase of 17.5% y-o-y compared to Q3 2011, drove up our estimates of European production, up 6.6% y-o-y. We have some reservations on the rapid pickup in Italian production as it run counter to our conversations with market participants; we will be investigating the sector further in the coming months. © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 8 of 19 Copper Monitor December 2012 www. crugroup.com ### Industry News #### Consumption - As part of ongoing restructuring efforts, Japanese wire and cable maker **Hitachi Cable** announced on 13th November that it will merge with sister company **Hitachi Metals** . The merged company will concentrate on "producing synergies" and expanding overseas sales, concentrating on "industrial and information infrastructure and automobile and electronicsrelated industries." The **Hitachi Group** as a whole has a target of generating 50% of sales outside of Japan, a figure which Hitachi Cables has yet to reach. - Shenzhen-listed wire and cable producer **Qingdao Hanhe Cable Co** announced on 27th November that it has won a contract to supp

ly cables to the **State Grid Corporation of China** as part of a fifth round of contract tendering.  The contract, worth RMB81.8M (US$13M), will involve supplying the 220KV cable as well as 20.304 KM of 500V cable.  In a separate announcement the company said it was selling its 51% stake in **Tianjin Hydraulic Machinery** and using the funds to invest in the research and development of competitive products. 

- **Kobelco** , a diversified Japanese group with interests ranging from copper to construction machinery, announced on 19<sup>th</sup> November that it is licensing one of its leading copper alloy products, used in terminals and connectors, to German firm **Wieland** .  The company said that the deal would allow it "to establish a global supply network for copper alloys, especially for automotive applications." This is the second time Kobelco have expanded their global presence in the copper alloys market through such an agreement:  The company licensed the same technology to **Aurubis Buffalo Inc** for US manufacturing and distribution in 2008. 

- **Yazaki Corporation** , the Japanese wire harness maker, announced recently that it has begun production at a new wire harness plant in the Koh Kong Special Economic Zone in Cambodia. The plant, which is part of a network of 40 global locations operated by Yazaki, is located in Cambodia to capitalise on low labour costs.  The Cambodian plant is also located in close proximity to Thailand which is one of the Japanese automobiles largest production bases outside of Japan.  In separate news, about 250 workers at the Yazaki’s wire harness plants in Shantou, Guangdong province, went on strike on 22<sup>nd</sup> November.  The strike followed an announcement that the company was going to move 1,200 workers from its Shantou site to another plant. 

- **General Cable Corporation** announced on 5<sup>th</sup> November that it had completed its acquisition of **Prestolite Wire LLC** , the wire & cable and wiring harnesses producer.  Prestolite Wire, which reported revenues of US$170M in 2011, has two production sites based in the USA and Mexico and manufactures predominately for the transport sector.  Commenting on the acquisition, General Cable said that the Prestolite Wire is "highly complementary to our existing transportation-related businesses as approximately 90% of Prestolite's revenues are generated from products that are incremental to the Company's existing product portfolio."

#### Mine Production 

- Mongolia’s vice-minister for mining, Erdenebulgan Oyun, announced on 5<sup>th</sup> November that a power purchase agreement (PPA) had been reached between Chinese electricity suppliers and mine operator Oyu Tolgoi LLC to supply power to the **Oyu Tolgoi** mining project after months of delays. The company expects a seven-week commissioning of the ore-processing equipment to begin

within the next few weeks, with the first commercial concentrate production in Q2 2013.  The mine will produce 470,000t/y of copper-in-concentrate at full production. 

- Following the early labour agreement at **Codelco’s** Andina mine, most unionised workers at the **Chuquicamata** mine have voted to start early negotiations ahead of their contract expiry at the end of February 2013.  Union representatives expect that an agreement will be reached in the first half of December, and are also expected to press for a longer contract than the current one of 38 months.  Chuquicamata produced 369,000t of copper-in-concentrate and 65,000t of EW cathode in 2011. 

- Workers at **Zambia** ’s copper mines are demanding wage increases of as much as 50% for 2013, according to the Mineworkers’ union of Zambia. Talks began in October and are expected to be concluded before the current agreements expire at the end of this year.  The talks affect workers 

###### at the **Glencore** -owned **Mopani** operations, **Vedanta** -owned **Konkola Copper Mines** and **Jinchuan Group** ’s **Chibuluma** mines. 

- **Peru** ’s congress has approved a bill to create an environmental agency ( **Senace** ), which will be in charge of evaluating environmental impact studies (EIS) instead of the energy and mines ministry.  The agency will be set up under the environment ministry ( **Minam** ), and bodies such as the health, economy and agriculture ministries will be involved in the evaluation process.  It is expected that Senace will begin operating in mid-2013.  Minam has also approved a new scale of fines for offences and penalties for the mining sector, including the fine for EIS infringement. The maximum fine has increased from 600UIT to 10,000UIT, where a UIT is a taxation unit worth about 3,650 soles (US$1,400). 

- **Codelco** has reported a year-on-year drop in profits and output for the first nine months of 2012 due to higher energy, fuel and other input costs, lower copper prices and lower ore grades. Production at its mines, excluding the El Abra joint venture and its share of Anglo American Sur, declined by 4.8% to 1.19Mt, largely due to lower ore grades at Chuquicamata.  Head grades at the mine fell from 0.96% to 0.78%, which was in line with projections as the pit is becoming exhausted.  Pre-tax profits declined by 39% from US$5.32B to US$3.26B. 

- **Mitsui and Co** is to increase its share in **Acrux** , the **Codelco/Mitsui** joint venture company that controls 29.5% of Anglo American Sur as part of a loan refinancing agreement.  Mitsui will take a further 15.25% of Acrux, giving it an additional 4.5% in Anglo American Sur.  The amount of

- The **Xstrata/Glencore** merger has moved closer to being completed with the approval of shareholders being gained on November 20<sup>th</sup> and the European Commission two days later.  The approval of the EU commission comes with the condition that Glencore scraps an exclusive zinc sales deal with **Nyrstar** and sells its share in the company.  The deal still requires regulatory approval in South Africa and China. 

#### Exploration and Development 

- **Xstrata Copper** has announced that its **Antapaccay** mine project in southern Peru began production of commercial grade concentrates at the beginning of November and has delivered its first shipment to Matarani Port for export.  Plant commissioning activities are continuing as the plant ramps up to the nameplate processing capacity of 70,000t/d of ore, which is expected to be achieved in the first half of 2013.  The mine will produce an average of 160,000t/y of copper in concentrates in the first few years of production.  It is located 10km from the **Tintaya** mine where mining operations are due to cease in the next few months due to reserve exhaustion.  The mineral resource at Antapaccay has recently been expanded and is now estimated to contain 5Mt of copper metal, sufficient to sustain operations at the current level for around 30 years. 

- The development of **Inmet Mining’s** 260,000t/y **Cobre Panama** project has moved ahead with the award of the EPC for the ore processing plant and supply contracts for 84 pieces of mobile mine equipment.   The contract for the processing plant has been awarded to Joint Venture Panama (JVP), led by SNC-Lavalin.  Construction is expected to begin in Q4 2013.  The mine equipment includes shovels and drilling equipment and is due to begin arriving in 2013 in time for the pre-stripping operations scheduled to commence in Q4 2014. 

- **Hudbay Minerals** has signed a five-year contract with Peruvian construction company **Graсa y Montero** (GyM) for earthworks and mine maintenance at its US$1.5B **Constancia** project in the Cuzco region of Peru.  The contract is worth approximately US$800M.  The company gave the go-ahead for the project in August 2012 and initial production is scheduled for late 2014, with full production of 85,000t/y expected to be achieved in Q2 2015. 

- **Vale** announced on 7<sup>th</sup> November that it had been granted an operating licence by Brazil’s environmental regulator **Ibama** for its 100,000t/y **Salobo II** copper project in Brazil’s northern state of Para.  The project is planned as an expansion to the recently commissioned Salobo I site, which has been operational since June.  Vale plans to commission Salobo II in H1 2014.

#### Smelting and Refining 

- **First Quantum Minerals** has received environmental approval from the Zambian environmental management agency for its planned 300,000t/y smelte

r at **Kansanshi** in Solwezi. In its Q3 2012 report, First Quantum reported that detailed design of the smelter is well progressed and all major equipment has been ordered. Earthworks construction is approximately 65% complete and installation is expected to begin in early 2013, with the completion of construction scheduled for mid-2014.   The smelter will treat concentrates from the Kansanshi mine and the 250,000t/y cu-in-concentrates **Sentinel** mine project, which received board approval in May 2012.  It will also supply acid to the Kansanshi leaching operations. 

- China’s **Tongling Nonferrous Metals** group has announced that it plans to produce 1.4Mt/y of refined copper by 2015 and 300,000t/y of semi-fabricated products.  Total refined copper production in 2011 was 854,000t.  A 400,000t/y expansion to 580,000t at the **Jinchang** plant is due to be completed at the end of 2012, and a 100,000t/y expansion to 300,000t/y at the **Zhangjiagang** anode plant and refinery in 2013.  A further 100,000t/y increase is planned, but no time scale has been announced. 

- In early November **Argentina** ’s mining minister, Jorge Mayoral, met with officials from NFC, a unit of **China Non Ferrous Metal Mining Group** to discuss a proposal to construct a copper smelter and refinery in Argentina.  The project would involve investing US$750M in a plant to produce 210,000t/y of refined copper and 700,000t/y of by-product sulphuric acid.  Currently there is one operating mine in Argentina, **Bajo de la Alumbrera** , which exports all of its concentrates to smelters in Asia and Europe.  Production in the country will rise if the development of the **Agua Rica** project, currently under feasibility study, goes ahead, and the government is pushing for more domestic processing of concentrates.
